description: Seed of the fastener-library stream (DRAFT_tolerance_stack_mvp groundwork item 1), now also holding vendor bearings under Joby source-control drawings. Every entry carries a `values_source` saying where its numbers came from -- a source_ref-shaped dict, mandatory unless `values_status` is `not_transcribed`, in which case it is explicitly null. It stays filled after a promotion to `library`, because where the inline numbers came from is still true and useful once they are a cross-check rather than the source. READ IT BEFORE REUSING A BAND: five of the fifteen entries transcribe the 260729 workbook (with parts-list nomenclature corroborating some nominals), which makes those numbers UNUSABLE as a source in a from-scratch stack -- citing the entry instead of the xlsx launders the same untraced value (SOP Step 5b, trap 17). SIX entries are traced and safe to reuse: the four NAS bolts, whose grips and ±.010 bands are printed on sheet 3 of `NAS6403-NAS6420 Rev 4.pdf` in the spec pile -- NAS6403U11D, whose values the spec library now owns (`values_status: library`), plus NAS6403U13H, NAS6403U14D and NAS6404U13D, re-sourced 2026-08-10 by handoff fastener_citations_and_confidence; and 214589-002 / 214588-002, traced to their own source-control drawings, where the drawing IS the controlling document for the vendor part and prints its limits directly. Four entries are `not_transcribed` with `values_source: null`. That the workbook-transcribed count fell from eight to five in one sitting is the finding worth carrying: those three bolts were re-sourceable from the day NAS6403-NAS6420 Rev 4.pdf landed in `data/inbox/specs/`, and nothing in the repo noticed that a new document had made an existing gap closable. That last clause stopped being true on 2026-08-13 (spec_pile_gap_join): `tests/debug_report_spec_pile_gaps.py` now joins every gap in this file and in the stack files against the pile, range-aware, and prints both the candidates and the documents still missing. Run it from the MAIN checkout -- the pile is gitignored, so in a worktree it skips loudly rather than reporting that nothing matches. Counts in this paragraph are asserted by tests/test_tolerance_stack.py::test_hardware_entry_values_source_counts_match_the_description, because a count written in prose goes stale silently -- as this one already did once. `library_ref` is the slot a real library entry drops into; when it is filled, `values_status` becomes `library` and the inline numbers become a cross-check rather than the source.

Added 2026-08-04 (pitch_link_stack), CORRECTED 2026-08-13 (spec_pile_gap_join): MS9363-09 also retains the 5-place PITCH-LINK joint in the same view (DETAIL B, balloon prefix 8X = 3 + 5), so it blocks two joints, not one. The bolt half of the alignment problem is CLOSED -- NAS6403 sheet 1 gives the cotter-hole position M = .174/.154 in from the point. THE NUT HALF IS CLOSED TOO, and had been for eight days when this correction was written. This clause read "What is still missing is entirely on the nut side: NUT HEIGHT, slot count, and slot depth", written 2026-08-04; `MS9363 Rev C.pdf` arrived in `data/inbox/specs/` on 2026-08-05 and was read into the spec library the same day, and it prints all three on sheet 1 TABLE I row -09: H = .178/.198 in (nut height), G = .084/.104 in (unslotted height, so slot depth is H - G), S = .073/.088 in (slot width), and the hex-face view's positional callout reads 6 PLACES (slot count). Re-read off a crop 2026-08-13 to confirm before rewriting this. Resolve them at spec-library subject MS9363-09; the entry itself stays `not_transcribed` on purpose, because no stack consumes it yet (tests/test_spec_library.py::test_only_the_one_entry_was_promoted). WHAT THE STALE CLAUSE WAS HIDING is the finding worth carrying: the parenthetical equating the missing geometry with "the thread-start-to-castellation spacing JPS00094 section 5.9.7 footnote (a) says varies between nuts" conflated two different things. The geometry is printed; the SPACING is not, by MS9363 or by anything else. Requirement 10 relates opposite slots to each other and the slot axis to the thread PD axis, and nothing on either sheet relates a slot to where the thread starts -- so the phase that decides which grips let a cotter hole line up with a slot is UNCONTROLLED, not unacquired. No better scan and no further document closes it; the remedy is the procedural one JPS00094 5.9.7 gives, capped at three washers by 5.5.3.a. This entry is therefore no longer a spec-library intake item at all.
Same as MS9363-09, for the VPA joint.

Resolve at spec-library subject MS9363-10. What remains here is the same uncontrolled quantity as on the -09: nothing in MS9363 relates a slot to the thread start, so the castellation phase is not acquirable and is handled procedurally per JPS00094 5.9.7.
